title: OwnMem daily telemetry archive
description: One UTC day of one installation's memory telemetry, reduced to counts and committed to Git. Local event files expire after thirty days and never leave the machine that wrote them, so this package is the only durable, portable record of how the system behaved on that day. It carries counts only: no query text, no query digest, no trace or snapshot identifier, no file path, no machine or account name, and no timestamp finer than `day`. Topic names are the single exception, because they are already public in the memory index this file sits beside.

installation_id.description: A one-way digest of the machine's local HMAC key. Identifies rows as coming from the same install without identifying the install.

partial_day.description: True when the day was still in progress at archive time. Set from the archiving clock, never re-derived by a reader, so every machine agrees on it.

window_id.description: The frozen protocol window this day belongs to. Always null in v1; the field exists so adding windows later does not reshape packages written before them.

stack_version.description: The recall stack that produced the day: the most common component_version across recall.completed, falling back to all events when the day had no recall.

day_head_commit.description: The last commit dated at or before the end of this UTC day: the build that was running while the day was collected. Anchoring to the day rather than to HEAD is what makes a finished day's package a pure function of (that day's events, the history up to that day). Anchored to HEAD, any later commit touching scripts/ silently rewrote every historical package.

tree_hash_basis.description: Which anchor produced scripts_tree_hash. A finished day resolves to the last commit of that day and never moves again; a day still in progress resolves to whatever HEAD was at archive time and will move. Stated rather than inferred from partial_day, because these are different claims about stability.

scripts_tree_hash.description: The scripts/ tree at day_head_commit. The hooks run that tree directly, so this is the code that collected the day.

released_version.description: The public package version declared at day_head_commit, not in the working tree. A day when 0.5.4 was current must not claim 0.5.5 because a later session bumped it.

release_marker_commit.description: The commit that first declared released_version, searched from day_head_commit rather than from HEAD: a release made after this day did not exist on it. It is the last point at which this tree and the published package were the same thing.

unreleased_delta.description: Whether the day's scripts/ tree differs from the tree at the release marker. Null when any link cannot be resolved -- no git, a shallow clone, an untracked manifest, a day older than the repository. Never inferred from the version string, because an unchanged version is not evidence of unchanged code.

legacy.description: Rows written before agent attribution existed. Reported apart because those days were genuinely mixed and no honest attribution can be recovered.

nested.description: Rows whose environment carried more than one host's markers. Counted apart rather than filed under this build's tie-break.

attempts.description: Recalls that were graded: session deduplication and legacy abstentions without a recorded reason are excluded, exactly as in the live report.

pairing_scope.description: A recall just before midnight and its delivery just after belong to two packages. Stated rather than left for a reader to infer from a rate that looks slightly low.

ledgers.description: Rows the three permanent ledgers gained on this day. They never expire, so a backfilled day reads them at full fidelity. The three are counted separately and may never be added together.

returned_topics.description: The topic names recall returned most often that day. Names, not bodies: they are already public in the memory index beside this file.
